title: Concatenating Parsed Pair Components
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $z$, $M$ halts within $c(|z|+1)$ steps and outputs the concatenation of the two components returned by the aligned pair parser when that parser succeeds, and outputs the empty word when it fails.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the parser-success concatenation, or the empty word on parser failure, within c(|z|+1) steps on every input
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes, within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the function
sending a word that encodes the pair $(a,b)$ under the self-delimiting pair
code to the concatenation $a b$, and any malformed word to the empty word.
